details.description: Medical Dictation is one of Google Cloud Speech-to-Text's two medical speech recognition models, alongside Medical Conversation, tuned for notes dictated by a single medical provider — for example, a doctor dictating notes about a patient's blood test results — and for vocabulary such as diagnoses, medications, symptoms, treatments, and conditions. It is offered through Speech-to-Text's v1 API and, per Google's documentation, is available only for US English.
advantages: Recognizes medical vocabulary — diagnoses, medications, symptoms, treatments, and conditions — that Google's general-purpose Speech-to-Text models are not tuned for.
Automatically enables spoken punctuation, formatting commands, and spoken headings, features Google's documentation says "cannot be disabled" for this model.

Supports automatic punctuation (enabled by default), alternate transcriptions, word timestamps, and word-level confidence, the only additional features Google's documentation allows with medical models.
disadvantages: Available only for US English (en-US); Google's documentation states medical models are not offered in any other language.
Listed only among Speech-to-Text's v1 API models; it does not appear among the v2 API's Chirp-based models (chirp_3, chirp_2, telephony) in Google's current documentation.
use_cases: Transcribing a single medical provider's dictated notes, such as a doctor recording findings from a patient's blood test.
Capturing medical documentation with correctly recognized diagnosis, medication, symptom, treatment, and condition terminology.
Structured dictation workflows that rely on spoken punctuation, spoken headings, and formatting commands to shape the transcript.

notes: Confirmed via Google's v1 and v2 model-name lists that medical_dictation exists only in the v1 API; catalog facts give no language, token, or deprecation constraints, and nothing here conflicts with them. Removed the allowlist-only claim: none of Google's medical-models, v1 transcription-model, v2 transcription-model, v1 product-overview, quotas, or best-practices pages state that medical_dictation requires allowlisting. The only allowlist reference found is an 'Allowlist-only features' nav heading marked 'Limited Access' whose contents are not publicly viewable, so it cannot be used to confirm the claim either way. Google's v1 transcription-model page does call medical_dictation 'a premium model that costs more than the standard rate,' which is a price detail and is left out per style rules. Checked WaaV's gateway source (local checkout) for whether it exposes this the same way: WaaV's Google STT integration (gateway/src/core/stt/google/) implements Google's v2 Speech-to-Text API only and passes the configured model string straight through with no v1 or medical-model-specific handling, so a v1-only model like medical_dictation is not confirmed to be reachable through WaaV's current Google STT provider — out of scope for this write-up, which describes Google's own model.
